prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were generally overoptimistic for large changes, though winning tests were often underpredicted.
Reordering sign-in (sign_in, reorder) consistently worked and proved helpful across 2 tests.
Adding a new finish screen (finish, new_screen) hurt performance or showed no clear effect across 2 tests.
Sign-in copy tweaks (sign_in, copy) and new adoption flows (adoption, new_flow) showed no clear effect across 2 tests each.
Evidence remains thin for all other change types (hints, incentives, redesigns, layout changes, and home wait info) due to single tests or mixed results.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: +0.7% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- adoption, wait_info: +2.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, incentive: -2.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, layout: +2.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, hint: -1.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, incentive: +2.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: -4.5% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- home, hint: +0.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, redesign: -3.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: +2.6% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, copy: -0.6% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.1%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 79.1%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 84.4%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 20.1%

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Move sign-in after custom photo upload: Move the sign-in screen to take place after photo upload and pet selection but before the adoption certificate screen. (why: Reordering sign-in later in the funnel has consistently shown strong performance in prior tests, allowing users to pick or create their pet first.)
1: [adoption, redesign] Pick friend screen carousel redesign: Redesign the pet selection screen to use a carousel layout featuring dynamic preview components for each pet option. (why: Adoption has a relatively low conversion rate (60.9%) and long completion times (median 89s / mean 1017s); a carousel layout makes pet browsing smoother.)
2: [adoption, new_flow] Interactive photo upload checklist flow: Convert photo upload into a guided checklist sub-flow with mascot instructions for custom pet creation. (why: Support emails highlight issues where custom pets fail or look wrong (3 emails), and adoption drop-off is high.)
3: [adoption, new_screen] Pre-waiting pet setup verification screen: Add a new confirmation screen before the waiting screen to display summary details of the adopted pet. (why: Adoption drop-off is 60.9% and users express confusion over pet creation output; a summary verification screen reassures users before processing.)
4: [home, wait_info] Waiting screen ready notification toggle: Enable a system notification toggle on the waiting screen so users get alerted when pet generation completes. (why: The home waiting step has a long mean duration (2336s) and 15.6% drop-off; notification options let users multitask without abandoning.)
5: [choose_path, layout] Story screen spotlight layout redesign: Update the story screen to a spotlight layout featuring a prominent animated pet hero element. (why: Choose_path has a high mean duration (514s); an engaging spotlight intro screen improves initial user momentum.)
6: [finish, hint] Home intro desktop controls tray hint: Add text and hint components on the final home intro screen explaining desktop tray access and pet interaction shortcuts. (why: 3 support tickets reported confusion about how to control, hide, or talk to the pet after onboarding, and 3 reported pet visibility issues.)
7: [home, wait_info] Waiting screen animated companion idle preview: Add an animated hatching pet preview component to the waiting screen while background generation finishes. (why: Waiting screen median time is 201s and mean time is 2336s; visual engagement prevents drop-off during generation.)
8: [choose_path, copy] Choose path screen headline copy refresh: Rewrite the choose_path screen headline and body to clearly distinguish preset adoption from custom photo creation. (why: Choose_path mean time is 514s, indicating hesitation when choosing between preset and photo custom paths.)

scores.note: Reordering sign-in later in the flow has a proven track record (+3.1% avg) across previous tests.
Adoption has high drop-off (39.1%), but redesign evidence remains thin.
Strong evidence from both funnel drop-off and support mail, but adoption new flows previously showed minimal impact (+0.7%).
Adding new verification screens historically degrades performance (-4.5%).
Home wait info changes have consistently yielded positive lift (+2.6%).
Layout adjustments on choose_path showed initial positive results (+2.5%), but evidence is based on 1 test.
High support ticket overlap, but finish step hints performed poorly in past testing (-1.5%).
Addresses high waiting duration with proven wait_info pattern (+2.6%), though implementation cost is higher.
Low cost copy tweak addressing hesitation, though copy changes usually have subtle effects.
